intent: A clockmaker's tour of the planet: the table, then the two islands at either end of a French day, then the giant that refused to split its clock.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which country has the MOST time zones?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which country has the most time zones?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: France. Not the hexagon on the map, but its islands around the world: 12 time zones.

lines.direction: pull back to show Europe and Russia; the table builds with France on top; the Russian flag-ball shrugs on 'Russia', the clock sticker drops on 'France'
lines.text: Russia stretches 11 across a single landmass. The United States, with its islands, also 11. France: 12.

lines.direction: swing across the Pacific; the Tahiti pin on 'Tahiti', the Wallis pin on 'Wallis'; a TAHITI / WALLIS split with the two UTC offsets; the sun sticker, then the moon on 'gap' — one country, dawn and dusk at once
lines.text: Its clocks run from Tahiti, at UTC minus 10, to Wallis and Futuna, at plus 12: a gap of 22 hours.

lines.direction: fly west to China; it lights in the dim second colour on 'China'; the 1 CLOCK card and the China tag on 'single'; the alarm-clock sticker pulses on 'everywhere'
lines.text: And China, nearly as wide as the United States, picked a single clock: Beijing time, everywhere.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
